chunks: From him, from his father, from Hariz, from Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Verily, when Allah, the Exalted, created Adam (peace be upon him), He breathed into him from His spirit, so he breathed with ease. When he finished his breath, He said: 'O Adam, rise to your Lord and prostrate to Him.' So he rose and prostrated. When he finished his prostration, He said: 'O Adam, did you see what you prostrated to?' He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'For indeed, it prostrated to Me.'

Then He said: 'O Adam, indeed you have a right in this prostration, and I have a right in this prostration.' Adam said: 'What is my right, O Lord?' He said: 'That you be the father of mankind, and that your offspring will be in Paradise and Hellfire.' Adam said: 'Then what is Your right, O Lord?' He said: 'That you worship Me and associate nothing with Me.'
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'This is the first thing Allah created from the servant, and the first thing he prostrated to Allah.'
ai.seo_question: What was the first act of worship performed by Adam and what covenant did it establish?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq contextualizes this narrative within the doctrine of *Alam al-Dharr* (the Realm of Souls), where the primordial covenant (*Mithaq*) was established, affirming Adam's role as the progenitor and the foundation of *Tawhid*. This event is pivotal in Shia theology for illustrating the innate recognition of divine authority (*Fitrah*) and the continuity of the covenant through the Prophets and Imams.
